title: Storage
icon: FolderOpen
description: "Buckets and files: upload, download, view, transform images, and control access with permissions."
---

import { ShieldCheck, Database, Users, Radio } from 'lucide-react';

Applad storage keeps your files in **buckets**. A bucket is a container with its
own settings (size limit, allowed file types, permissions) and the files you
upload into it. You get metadata for every file (name, MIME type, size, a
content signature), direct download and inline-view endpoints, and on-the-fly
image transformations, all behind the same `/v1` API and SDKs as the rest of
Applad.

Every storage endpoint requires an authenticated caller: a client sends the
session bearer token (see [authentication](/build/authentication)), a server sends its
API key (`x-applad-key`). Both send the project header `x-applad-project`.

![The console Storage tab listing a project's buckets](/screens/storage.png)
_Files live in buckets, each with its own size limit, allowed types and permissions._

## Create a bucket

Create a bucket before you upload anything. You can pass a `bucketId` of your
own or let Applad generate one with `unique()`.

<Tabs items={['JavaScript', 'Dart']}>
<Tab value="JavaScript">
```ts
const bucket = await client.storage.createBucket('avatars', {
  bucketId: 'avatars',
  permissions: ['read("any")', 'create("users")'],
  maximumFileSize: 5 * 1024 * 1024,
  allowedFileExtensions: ['jpg', 'png', 'webp'],
});
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="Dart">
```dart
final storage = client.storage;

final bucket = await storage.createBucket(
  name: 'avatars',
  bucketId: 'avatars',
  permissions: ['read("any")', 'create("users")'],
  maximumFileSize: 5 * 1024 * 1024,       // 5 MB, in bytes
  allowedFileExtensions: ['jpg', 'png', 'webp'],
);
```
</Tab>
</Tabs>

Underlying route: `POST /v1/storage/buckets`. The response is the bucket:

```json
{
  "$id": "avatars",
  "$createdAt": "2026-07-28T10:00:00Z",
  "$updatedAt": "2026-07-28T10:00:00Z",
  "name": "avatars",
  "enabled": true,
  "$permissions": ["read(\"any\")", "create(\"users\")"],
  "maximumFileSize": 5242880,
  "allowedFileExtensions": ["jpg", "png", "webp"],
  "compression": "none",
  "encryption": false,
  "antivirus": false,
  "fileSecurity": false,
  "imageTransformations": true
}
```

### Bucket configuration

Every setting is optional on create; the table gives the type and the default
Applad applies when you omit it.

| Field | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | string | (required) | Human-readable bucket name. The only required field. |
| `bucketId` | string | generated | Your own id, or omit / pass `unique()` to have one generated. |
| `maximumFileSize` | integer (bytes) | `0` | Per-file cap. `0` means no bucket-level limit (the 500 MB hard ceiling still applies). |
| `allowedFileExtensions` | string array | `[]` | Allow-list of extensions (`jpg`) or MIME types (`image/jpeg`). Empty allows any type; an entry of `*` allows all. |
| `permissions` | string array | `[]` | Bucket-wide access rules (see [Permissions](#permissions)). |
| `fileSecurity` | boolean | `false` | When `true`, each file may also carry its own permissions. |
| `imageTransformations` | boolean | `true` | Advertises whether image previews may be transformed. Stored on the bucket; the preview endpoint does not currently gate on it. |
| `compression` | string | `"none"` | Stored on the bucket. See [the caveat](#storage-drivers). |
| `encryption` | boolean | `false` | Stored on the bucket. See [the caveat](#storage-drivers). |
| `antivirus` | boolean | `false` | Stored on the bucket. See [Antivirus scanning](#antivirus-scanning). |

<Callout title="maximumFileSize is enforced on the stream">
  The bucket cap is applied to the upload stream itself, not to the
  `Content-Length` the client claims. If the bucket's `maximumFileSize` is
  smaller than the 500 MB hard ceiling, the stream is cut at the bucket limit
  and the partial write is deleted, so a client cannot understate its size to
  slip a large file past the cap.
</Callout>

`allowedFileExtensions` matches case-insensitively against either the file's
extension or its MIME type, so `['jpg', 'image/png']` accepts both a `.jpg` by
name and any `image/png` by content type. File names are sanitised on upload:
directory components are stripped and the name is truncated to 255 characters.

List, fetch and update buckets with `listBuckets()` / `getBucket(id)` /
`updateBucket(...)` (`GET`/`PUT /v1/storage/buckets` and `/{bucketId}`), and
remove one with `deleteBucket(id)` (`DELETE /v1/storage/buckets/{bucketId}`).
`updateBucket` merges: any field you omit keeps its current value, so you can
flip a single flag (for example `enabled: false`) without resending the rest.
Deleting a bucket removes its files with it.

## Upload a file

Upload sends a multipart form with the file bytes, an optional `fileId`, and
optional per-file `permissions`.

Underlying route: `POST /v1/storage/buckets/{bucketId}/files` (multipart:
`file`, `fileId`, `permissions`).

<Tabs items={['JavaScript', 'Dart', 'cURL']}>
<Tab value="JavaScript">
```ts
// `file` is a browser File or Blob
const uploaded = await client.storage.createFile('avatars', file, 'me.png', {
  fileId: 'unique()',
  permissions: ['read("any")'],
});
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="Dart">
```dart
final file = await storage.createFile(
  bucketId: 'avatars',
  fileName: 'me.png',
  fileBytes: bytes,                 // List<int>
  fileId: 'unique()',              // or your own id
  mimeType: 'image/png',
  permissions: ['read("any")'],
);
print(file['\$id']);
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="cURL">
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.applad.io/v1/storage/buckets/avatars/files \
  -H "x-applad-project: <projectId>" \
  -H "x-applad-key: <apiKey>" \
  -F "fileId=unique()" \
  -F "file=@me.png"
```
</Tab>
</Tabs>

The response is the file's metadata:

```json
{
  "$id": "68a1...",
  "bucketId": "avatars",
  "$createdAt": "2026-07-28T10:01:00Z",
  "$updatedAt": "2026-07-28T10:01:00Z",
  "name": "me.png",
  "signature": "9f86d081...",
  "mimeType": "image/png",
  "sizeOriginal": 20481,
  "$permissions": ["read(\"any\")"]
}
```

Uploads are rejected with `413` (`storage_file_too_large`) past the bucket's
`maximumFileSize`, and with a `400` when the file type is not in the bucket's
`allowedFileExtensions`. There is a hard 500 MB ceiling per upload regardless of
bucket settings.

A single-shot upload is streamed straight to the storage driver while its
content signature (an MD5 digest, returned as `signature`) is computed in
passing, so a 500 MB upload does not cost 500 MB of memory. The exception is a
bucket with `antivirus` on: ClamAV needs the whole payload, so those uploads are
buffered before scanning (see [Antivirus scanning](#antivirus-scanning)).

### Large files: chunked upload

For large files, upload in chunks. This is a three-step flow over `/v1` routes;
the client SDKs do not wrap it yet, so call the routes directly.

<Steps>
<Step>
### Init

Declare the file and get its `fileId`:

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.applad.io/v1/storage/buckets/avatars/files/chunked \
  -H "x-applad-project: <projectId>" -H "x-applad-key: <apiKey>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"name":"video.mp4","mimeType":"video/mp4","size":52428800}'
# -> {"fileId":"...","uploadUrl":"/v1/storage/buckets/avatars/files/<fileId>/chunks"}
```
</Step>
<Step>
### Upload each chunk

Send each chunk to that URL with `PATCH`, numbering it with the `chunk`
query parameter (0-based). Each chunk is capped at 10 MB.

```bash
curl -X PATCH "https://api.applad.io/v1/storage/buckets/avatars/files/<fileId>/chunks?chunk=0" \
  -H "x-applad-project: <projectId>" -H "x-applad-key: <apiKey>" \
  --data-binary @chunk-0.bin
```
</Step>
<Step>
### Complete

Assemble the file:

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.applad.io/v1/storage/buckets/avatars/files/<fileId>/chunks/complete \
  -H "x-applad-project: <projectId>" -H "x-applad-key: <apiKey>"
```
</Step>
</Steps>

Complete returns the same file metadata shape as a normal upload.

## List and get files

<Tabs items={['JavaScript', 'Dart']}>
<Tab value="JavaScript">
```ts
const page = await client.storage.listFiles('avatars', { limit: 25, offset: 0 });
const meta = await client.storage.getFile('avatars', fileId);
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="Dart">
```dart
final page = await storage.listFiles(bucketId: 'avatars', limit: 25, offset: 0);
print(page['total']);
for (final f in page['files']) {
  print(f['name']);
}

final meta = await storage.getFile(bucketId: 'avatars', fileId: fileId);
```
</Tab>
</Tabs>

Routes: `GET /v1/storage/buckets/{bucketId}/files` (paginated with `limit` and
`offset`, default `limit` 25) returns `{ "total": n, "files": [...] }`;
`GET /v1/storage/buckets/{bucketId}/files/{fileId}` returns one file's metadata.

## Download and view

Two endpoints return the file's bytes. **Download** sets a
`Content-Disposition: attachment` header (the browser saves it); **view** serves
it inline (`Content-Disposition: inline`), which is what you want for an `<img>`
`src` or a preview.

<Tabs items={['JavaScript', 'Dart']}>
<Tab value="JavaScript">
```ts
const blob = await client.storage.downloadFile('avatars', fileId);
const inline = await client.storage.viewFile('avatars', fileId);
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="Dart">
```dart
final bytes = await storage.downloadFile(bucketId: 'avatars', fileId: fileId);
final inline = await storage.viewFile(bucketId: 'avatars', fileId: fileId);
```
</Tab>
</Tabs>

Routes: `GET /v1/storage/buckets/{bucketId}/files/{fileId}/download` and
`.../view`.

## Image transformations

The **preview** endpoint returns a file transformed on the fly. It is meant for
images; ask for a resized thumbnail, a different format, or a rotated crop with
query parameters. If the file is not an image (or you pass no transformation
parameters), the original bytes are served unchanged.

<Tabs items={['Dart', 'cURL']}>
<Tab value="Dart">
```dart
// There is no SDK wrapper; use the client's Dio instance directly.
// GET /v1/storage/buckets/{bucketId}/files/{fileId}/preview
final thumb = await client.dio.get(
  '/v1/storage/buckets/avatars/files/$fileId/preview',
  queryParameters: {'width': 200, 'height': 200, 'gravity': 'center'},
  options: Options(responseType: ResponseType.bytes),
);
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="cURL">
```bash
curl "https://api.applad.io/v1/storage/buckets/avatars/files/<fileId>/preview?width=200&height=200&output=jpg&quality=80" \
  -H "x-applad-project: <projectId>" -H "x-applad-key: <apiKey>" \
  -o thumb.jpg
```
</Tab>
</Tabs>

Supported query parameters:

| Parameter | Values | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `width`, `height` | pixels | Resize. Give one to scale proportionally, or both. |
| `gravity` | `center`, `top`, `bottom`, `left`, `right`, `top-left`, `top-right`, `bottom-left`, `bottom-right` | Which part to keep when cropping to both `width` and `height`. |
| `output` | `png`, `jpg` | Output format. |
| `quality` | `1`–`100` | JPEG quality (default 85). |
| `rotation` | `90`, `180`, `270` | Rotate. |
| `borderWidth` + `borderColor` | pixels + hex (`ff0000`) | Draw a border. |
| `borderRadius` | pixels | Round the corners. |
| `opacity` | `1`–`99` | Blend with transparency. |
| `background` | hex (`ffffff`) | Fill behind transparent areas. |

Transformations are applied in a fixed order, so combined parameters compose
predictably: resize (with gravity crop) then rotate then border radius then
border then opacity then background fill then encode. When you pass both `width`
and `height` with a non-centre `gravity`, the image is first cropped to the
requested aspect ratio from that anchor, then scaled. `borderColor` and
`background` accept a 3- or 6-digit hex string with or without a leading `#`;
an unparseable colour falls back to black.

The preview endpoint sets `Cache-Control: public, max-age=86400` on a
transformed response, so a CDN or browser can cache a thumbnail for a day. If
transformation fails (the bytes are not a decodable image), the original file is
served unchanged rather than erroring, so a `.pdf` in an image bucket still
downloads through `/preview`.

<Callout title="Formats">
  `output` encodes to PNG or JPEG. Any other value (including `webp`) falls back
  to JPEG. Decoding covers PNG, JPEG and GIF inputs. Resizing uses
  nearest-neighbour scaling, which is fast but not the sharpest, so preview is
  best for thumbnails and avatars rather than pixel-perfect resampling.
</Callout>

## Delete a file

<Tabs items={['JavaScript', 'Dart']}>
<Tab value="JavaScript">
```ts
await client.storage.deleteFile('avatars', fileId);
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="Dart">
```dart
await storage.deleteFile(bucketId: 'avatars', fileId: fileId);
```
</Tab>
</Tabs>

Route: `DELETE /v1/storage/buckets/{bucketId}/files/{fileId}` (returns `204`).
This removes both the stored bytes and the metadata record.

## Permissions

Buckets and files use the same `action("role")` permission strings as
[databases](/build/databases) and the shared [permissions](/build/permissions) model. The
actions are `read`, `create`, `update` and `delete`; roles include `any`,
`users`, `user:<id>` and `team:<id>`.

- Set **bucket** permissions (`permissions` on the bucket) for rules that apply
  to every file in it, for example `read("any")` on a bucket of public assets.
- Turn on **`fileSecurity`** and pass `permissions` when you upload, so each file
  also carries its own rules. Both a bucket's `$permissions` and a file's
  `$permissions` come back on read.

Every storage route requires an authenticated session or API key, so files are
never served anonymously by default. To hand out one private file without a
session, mint a **signed URL**: a time-limited token the view and download
routes accept via a `?token=` query parameter.

```bash
# Mint a token (default TTL 3600s):
curl -X POST https://api.applad.io/v1/storage/buckets/avatars/files/<fileId>/signed \
  -H "x-applad-project: <projectId>" -H "x-applad-key: <apiKey>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"expiresIn": 600}'
# -> {"token":"<token>"}

# Then fetch without auth headers, using the token:
curl "https://api.applad.io/v1/storage/buckets/avatars/files/<fileId>/view?token=<token>"
```

The token is bound to its project, bucket and file and expires, so it cannot be
replayed against another file or after its TTL. It is signed with HMAC-SHA256
over the project, bucket, file and expiry, using the instance's `JWT_SECRET`.
A token that carries a different project context than the request is rejected,
so it cannot be lifted into another project.

<Callout title="A downloaded file is named by its id">
  The `download` endpoint sets `Content-Disposition: attachment` with the file's
  generated id as the filename, not its original `name`. If you need the
  original name on disk, set it client-side from the file's metadata.
</Callout>

## Storage drivers

Where the bytes physically live is an instance-wide choice, set with the
`STORAGE_DRIVER` environment variable. It is transparent to the API and SDKs:
the same routes behave identically whichever driver is active.

<Tabs items={['Local disk', 'S3-compatible']}>
<Tab value="Local disk">
The default (`STORAGE_DRIVER=local`). Files are written under `STORAGE_PATH`
(default `/var/applad/storage`) at `<projectId>/<bucketId>/<fileId>`. Every
path is verified to stay within the storage root before a read, write or
delete, so a crafted file id cannot escape into the host filesystem.
</Tab>
<Tab value="S3-compatible">
Set `STORAGE_DRIVER=s3` to store objects in any S3-compatible service (AWS S3,
MinIO, Cloudflare R2, and so on). Requests are signed with AWS Signature V4.

| Variable | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `S3_BUCKET` | (empty) | Target object-store bucket. |
| `S3_REGION` | `us-east-1` | Region used for signing and the default endpoint. |
| `S3_ENDPOINT` | AWS regional | Override for MinIO / R2 / other providers. |
| `S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID` | (empty) | Access key. |
| `S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` | (empty) | Secret key. |

Object keys mirror the local layout: `<projectId>/<bucketId>/<fileId>`.
</Tab>
</Tabs>

## At-rest processing

A bucket's `compression`, `encryption` and `antivirus` flags are enforced on
upload. Compression and encryption transform only the stored bytes: the `size`
and `signature` Applad reports always describe the original file, and every read
path (download, inline `view`, signed-URL `view`, and image transforms) reverses
the transforms transparently, so a client always receives the exact bytes that
were uploaded.

<Callout title="Toggling a flag never corrupts existing files">
  How a file was encoded is recorded per file, not read from the bucket's
  current flags, so turning `compression` or `encryption` on or off later never
  mis-decodes files already stored under the previous setting. Existing files
  keep reading correctly; only new uploads follow the new setting.
</Callout>

### Compression

Turn a bucket's `compression` flag on to gzip file bytes at rest. No instance
configuration is required, and reads decompress on the fly. Compression trades a
little CPU for less disk or object-store usage and helps most on text-like
content; already-compressed formats such as JPEG, PNG or ZIP gain little.

### Encryption

Turn a bucket's `encryption` flag on to store files as AES-GCM ciphertext. This
needs an instance key:

| Variable | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `STORAGE_ENCRYPTION_KEY` | Hex string decoding to 16, 24 or 32 bytes (AES-128/192/256). Generate with `openssl rand -hex 32`. |

A fresh random nonce is stored with each file, so two identical uploads produce
different ciphertext. If a bucket has `encryption` on while no key is configured,
uploads are rejected rather than written in the clear. Keep the key safe and
stable: losing or changing it makes existing encrypted files unreadable. When
both flags are on, a file is compressed first and then encrypted.

## Antivirus scanning

Set `CLAMAV_ADDR` to a running `clamd` TCP address (for example `clamav:3310`)
to enable scanning; the bundled ClamAV service is off by default and starts with
`docker compose --profile antivirus up`. With a scanner configured, uploads to a
bucket with `antivirus` on are scanned before they are stored. Applad talks to
`clamd` over its TCP `INSTREAM` interface, streaming the payload in chunks and
reading back the verdict. A clean file is written normally; an infected file is
rejected and never persisted. Because the scanner needs the complete payload, an
antivirus-enabled upload is buffered in memory rather than streamed, still
subject to the same size caps. A bucket with `antivirus` off is never scanned,
even when a scanner is configured.
